articles.title: 10 Schema Types for Technical SEO and AI Search
articles.excerpt: I've seen technical SEO discussions focus heavily on whether schema markup is valid. I think the more interesting question is whether it tells the right story about the business. Imagine a search engi…
articles.body: I've seen technical SEO discussions focus heavily on whether schema markup is valid. I think the more interesting question is whether it tells the right story about the business. Imagine a search engine trying to connect these dots: Who published this article? Which organization does the author work for? What product is being discussed? How does this page fit into the website? Is the information consistent across the site? Your schema markup can pass a validation test without answering those questions well. A business might have multiple versions of its name across pages. An author might have no clear connection to their articles. Product markup might describe a price that's no longer available. These aren't always syntax problems. They're information architecture problems.
articles.author: Sayed Sayeedur Rahman

articles.title: Sleep Peacefully. Wake Up Informed: How I Built Sloth Digest with Local AI
articles.excerpt: *This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 3: Slow and Steady Modern communication tools have turned our mornings into an anxiety trap. Between student councils, hackath…
articles.body: *This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 3: Slow and Steady What I Built Modern communication tools have turned our mornings into an anxiety trap. Between student councils, hackathon teams, and family WhatsApp groups, waking up often means confronting 300 to 500 unread messages: inside jokes, reaction emoji, pizza memes, and fragmented logistics. Finding whether someone actually asked you a question or set a deadline requires 35 to 45 minutes of compulsive, thumb-numbing scrolling. I built Sloth Digest — an offline-first, local-first web application that reads your busy group chats overnight on your own computer so you wake up completely calm.

articles.excerpt: Auracast es la función de difusión de Bluetooth LE Audio: en lugar de emparejar un móvil con cada oyente, una fuente emite una transmisión y cualquier receptor compatible puede unirse a ella. Sirve pa…
articles.body: Auracast es la función de difusión de Bluetooth LE Audio: en lugar de emparejar un móvil con cada oyente, una fuente emite una transmisión y cualquier receptor compatible puede unirse a ella. Sirve para compartir el audio del teléfono con varias personas o para escuchar la emisión de una sala, una conferencia o una zona de espera. El problema es saber si tu equipo lo soporta de verdad. Antes de comprar conviene revisar: El número de versión no basta. Que la ficha diga «Bluetooth 5.2» o superior no confirma Auracast; la función tiene que aparecer de forma expresa para ese modelo y variante. Cada extremo se comprueba por separado. Unos auriculares compatibles no convierten el móvil o la tele en emisor, y un transmisor Auracast no sirve con auriculares que no pueden unirse a una emisión.

articles.title: Zero-Hallucination Reverse Proxies for AI DevOps: Building a Caddyfile Connector for Cognee
articles.excerpt: Autonomous AI DevOps and site reliability engineering (SRE) agents—such as Claude Code, Devin, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot—are increasingly being used to diagnose routing issues, configure SSL certific…
articles.body: Autonomous AI DevOps and site reliability engineering (SRE) agents—such as Claude Code, Devin, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot—are increasingly being used to diagnose routing issues, configure SSL certificates, and manage reverse proxies for microservices. But there's a catch: an AI agent can generate a plausible configuration without knowing how your infrastructure is actually configured. That gap can lead to problems such as: Port confusion: Routing requests to localhost:8000 when the service actually listens on port 8080 . Incorrect path matching: Confusing Caddy's named matchers, such as @api , with directives such as handle_path , or overlooking when a path prefix needs to be stripped.

articles.title: WordPress Speed Tips: Make Your Site Load Fast (Even on Shared Hosting)
articles.excerpt: A slow WordPress site loses visitors before they read a single word. Studies consistently show that most visitors leave if a page takes more than a few seconds to load, and Google uses speed as a rank…
articles.body: A slow WordPress site loses visitors before they read a single word. Studies consistently show that most visitors leave if a page takes more than a few seconds to load, and Google uses speed as a ranking signal too. The good news: most WordPress sites are slow for a handful of fixable reasons, not because they need an expensive server. Here are the fixes that actually move the needle, in the order that matters most. 1. Start with the heaviest thing: your images Unoptimised images are the single most common cause of a slow WordPress site. A photo straight from a phone can be several megabytes; a web page should rarely serve an image larger than a few hundred kilobytes. Resize images to the size they actually display at (a 1200px-wide hero image does not need to be 4000px wide).

articles.title: A Practical Framework for GEO (Generative Engine Optimization)
articles.excerpt: Most teams are still trying to apply classic SEO tactics to an AI-first internet. But when your buyers type questions into ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity or Gemini instead of Google, the job changes. You…
articles.body: Most teams are still trying to apply classic SEO tactics to an AI-first internet. But when your buyers type questions into ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity or Gemini instead of Google, the job changes. You’re no longer just ranking pages; you’re trying to become the safest, clearest answer those models can give. That’s what GEO — Generative Engine Optimization — is about. In this article, I’ll break down a practical GEO framework you can use without buying anything: how to audit your AI visibility, close the biggest gaps, and measure progress over time. 1. Think in entities, not just pages Search engines index pages. AI engines reason about entities: brands, people, products, categories.

articles.title: Your agent installs packages before anyone vets them. I built a gate that runs first.
articles.excerpt: Your agent installs packages before anyone vets them. I built a gate that runs first. My coding agent resolves a task, picks a package, and runs the install. The postinstall hook fires before I read a…
articles.body: Your agent installs packages before anyone vets them. I built a gate that runs first. My coding agent resolves a task, picks a package, and runs the install. The postinstall hook fires before I read any output. By the time a post-install audit, a PR check, or a dashboard tells me something was wrong, the payload has already run. That is the moment I wanted to gate: after the agent has chosen the artifact, before the install or run command executes. What I built vetgate is a local, deterministic pre-execution gate. It is an MCP server and a CLI mirror. Call it instead of running the install: one call, one verdict ( ALLOW , DENY , or REVIEW ), every finding carrying the exact evidence string it matched, and a manifest that makes the verdict re-checkable without re-running anything.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 25, 1671: Astronomer Giovanni Cassini discovers Iapetus, Saturn's 'yin-yang' moon
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 25, 1671, the Italian astronomer Giovanni Cassini discovered a new moon at Saturn! Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 25, 1671, the Italian astronomer Giovanni Cassini discovered a new moon at Saturn! Iapetus was the second moon anyone had ever found orbiting Saturn, and it was the first of four moons Cassini would discover at the ringed planet. The Dutch astronomer Christiaan Huygens had discovered Titan , the largest of Saturn's moons, about six years earlier. After Cassini found Iapetus, he also found the moons Rhea, Tethys and Dione. When Cassini first saw Iapetus, the moon looked like a tiny speck on the west side of Saturn. He calculated its orbit and thought he would be able to see it again on the east side of Saturn 39 days later, but it was nowhere to be seen.

articles.body: On Thursday, Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro signed the Artificial Intelligence Deceptive Advertising Act into law, requiring disclosures on AI-generated ads. The law requires any ad - whether it's a still image, video, audio, or text - that "has been significantly modified or generated by artificial intelligence" to include a label in the same format as the ad itself. That applies to TV commercials from multi-billion-dollar companies , as well as restaurants' ugly, crowded flyers about their wing specials. articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 24, 1946: V-2 rocket takes 1st photos of Earth from space
articles.excerpt: On October 24, 1946, a V-2 rocket captured the first-ever photo of Earth from space. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On October 24, 1946, a V-2 rocket captured the first-ever photo of Earth from space. While these grainy, black-and-white images might not look like much today, they were a huge deal at the time, because no one had ever seen Earth from space before. The V-2 rocket launched from the White Sands Missile Range in New Mexico. It carried a 35-millimeter motion picture camera that captured a new frame every second and a half. The rocket soared to an altitude of about 65 miles before falling back to Earth. Both the rocket and the camera were destroyed after crashing into the Earth at a speed of about 340 miles per hour. But the film survived because it was protected inside a steel case. Scientists had to drive out into the New Mexico desert to retrieve the film.

articles.title: 'Star Trek: Strange New Worlds' was afraid to say anything in season of gimmicks
articles.excerpt: The fourth season of "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds" was one giant gimmick: shoving "Trek" into as many genres as possible and often directly adapting classic films from those genres.
articles.body: It didn’t take long for fans to figure out that the fourth season of "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds" was going to be unlike any season of " Star Trek " before it. The entire season was one giant gimmick, and that gimmick was shoving "Trek" into as many genres as possible and often directly adapting classic films from those genres. You could argue that an entire season of gimmick episodes is a bold risk: putting the characters in fun, wacky situations to see how they react. It could be interesting, but the season we got never made the most of the concept. It was all so safe and paint-by-numbers, and, most importantly, it didn't have anything profound or interesting to say. That should trouble any Trekkie.

Over millennia, the night sky has helped shape human beliefs.
